title: Federal research ambition runs through industrial capacity
summary: A qualitative map connecting DARPA research direction, government-wide R&D priorities, AI infrastructure, transmission need, secure supply chains, and eight stage-bounded implementation trails.
map_question: What must exist between federal research ambition and a secure, scalable operating capability?
interpretation_boundary: The map connects explicit source relationships, reviewed synthesis signals, and named implementation records. Awards, obligations, scheduled trials, delivered material, and standards artifacts remain distinct from completed facilities, accepted systems, operating infrastructure, or scaled outcomes.

nodes.label: DARPA and federal R&D direction
nodes.note: Budget guidance and research portfolios identify the capability fields and their enabling systems.

nodes.label: DARPA supply-chain and logistics portfolio
nodes.note: The portfolio treats making, maintaining, supply chains, logistics, and megasystem resilience as research work.

nodes.label: Materials, tools, and production capacity
nodes.note: Usable capability depends on processing, equipment, manufacturing, suppliers, workforce, and sustainment.

nodes.label: Secure compute and reliable power
nodes.note: AI adoption is tied to chips, secure data centers, power, assurance, acquisition, and supply chains.

nodes.label: Transmission planning and delivery
nodes.note: DOE identifies new transmission need associated with data centers, manufacturing, and large loads.

nodes.label: Resilient industrial base
nodes.note: Security strategies and policy actions converge on materials, production, cyber, energy, communications, and supplier resilience.

nodes.label: Implementation evidence
nodes.note: Eight records now establish partial implementation trails, but later construction, test, acceptance, operation, and scale gates remain open.

nodes.label: Named performers and scheduled field trial
nodes.note: The Lift Challenge names invited teams and an August 2026 trial without pre-claiming the results.

nodes.label: Awards, obligations, and contracts
nodes.note: Talon, MP Materials, NAPMP, Southline, and OpenAI records identify instruments and amounts while separating value, obligation, outlay, and delivery.

nodes.label: Produced and delivered project material
nodes.note: Project Pele's first TRISO fuel batch reached the demonstration site, upstream of reactor startup and operation.

nodes.label: Testbed and standards artifacts
nodes.note: NIST records testbed software, laboratory infrastructure, and accepted O-RAN contributions without claiming a completed 6G system.

links.note: Government-wide priorities and DARPA's portfolio overlap across AI, compute, manufacturing, energy, materials, and security.
The budget and office descriptions explicitly include making, maintaining, tooling, materials, supply chains, and logistics.
Secure AI infrastructure depends on chips, equipment, data centers, suppliers, and workforce.
DOE identifies hyperscale data centers and manufacturing as drivers of transmission need.
The policy stack treats secure material and production capacity as an industrial-base requirement.
Reliable power supports resilient capability, but the draft study does not prove specific projects or delivery.
Named implementation records now exist, but they do not establish completed or scaled capability.
Phase 55L adds selected award, obligation, trial, milestone, procurement, and standards records; later transition and operating evidence remains necessary.
The Lift Challenge provides named performers and a dated trial inside DARPA's logistics and aviation research activity.
Official award, obligation, loan, capacity-contract, and prototype-agreement records establish named financial actions.
Project Pele fuel production and delivery provide bounded physical evidence before reactor operation.
NIST's testbed, software, and incorporated contributions provide standards and test infrastructure evidence.

what_this_map_supports: Federal research direction can be analyzed as a dependency stack rather than a list of technologies.
The source set explicitly connects research with materials, manufacturing, supply chains, power, compute, cyber, and resilience.
Implementation evidence is a separate gate from strategy, budget requests, and solicitations.
Named records can be placed on a stage ladder without treating awards, obligations, scheduled tests, or delivered material as operating outcomes.
what_this_map_does_not_prove: It does not prove enacted funding, successful research, production readiness, supplier security, grid delivery, or operational adoption.
It does not rank technologies, programs, regions, or suppliers.
It does not create a numeric 42/59 score.
next_records_needed: FY2027 appropriations and DARPA award records tied to the Phase 55K portfolio.
Completed Lift Challenge results, measured performance, prize actions, transition agreements, and procurement records.
Facility, equipment, commissioning, qualification, supplier, workforce, and production evidence behind Talon, MP Materials, and NAPMP.
Current Southline permits, financing, construction, interconnection, and energization records.
Project Pele startup and test evidence, OpenAI prototype delivery and acceptance records, and later wireless test, standards, certification, and deployment artifacts.
